And the number of points $P_c$ must be at least $m_c$.
The total number of colors is $\sum n_{m_c}$.
$\sum n_{m_c} \cdot m_c \le n^3$.
To maximize $\sum n_{m_c}$, we want $m_c$ to be as small as possible for each point.
For a point $(x, y, z)$, $m_c$ is the size of the set $I_x(c)$.
But $x \in I_x(c)$, $y \in I_y(c)$, $z \in I_z(c)$.
Since $I_x(c), I_y(c), I_z(c)$ are just permutations of each other, they all have the same size $m_c$.
And $m_c \ge \max(\text{distinct values in } \{x, y, z\})$.
- If $x=y=z$, then $m_c \ge 1$.
- If exactly two are same, $m_c \ge 2$.
- If all three are different, $m_c \ge 3$.
This is exactly what I used!

And we found a partition that achieves these minimums.
